senses.definition: To hit or close something with great force and usually a loud sound.
senses.example: The wind slammed the screen door shut.

senses.definition: To lean or slope at an angle.
senses.example: Our lines began to slant when we tried writing without a ruler.

senses.definition: An angle or slope away from the level or upright position.
senses.example: The roof had a steep slant.

senses.definition: To hit or land against something with a flat surface and make a sharp sound.
senses.example: The big wave slapped the side of the boat.

senses.definition: A slanted line such as the mark between numbers in a fraction.
senses.example: My teacher drew a slash between the numerator and the denominator.

senses.definition: To cut across something quickly or make an amount much smaller.
senses.example: The store slashed the price of the last few notebooks.

senses.definition: A vehicle without wheels that slides over snow or ice, often on narrow supports called runners.
senses.example: We pulled the sled back up the snowy hill.

senses.definition: To ride on a sled for fun or travel.
senses.example: We sledded down the little hill behind the park.

senses.definition: To be in the natural resting state in which you are less aware of things around you and may dream.
senses.example: I slept until the birds started to sing.

senses.definition: The natural period of rest when a person or animal is asleep.
senses.example: A night of good sleep helped me feel ready for school.

senses.definition: In U.S. weather reports, small ice pellets that fall from clouds.
senses.example: Bits of sleet bounced when they hit the front steps.

senses.definition: To fall as small pellets of ice.
senses.example: It began sleeting while we were still inside the library.

senses.definition: The part of clothing that covers some or all of an arm.
senses.example: I rolled up my sleeve before washing the brush.

senses.definition: A thin cover made to slide around something.
senses.example: I put the old record back in its paper sleeve.

senses.definition: A flat piece cut from a larger thing, usually fairly thin.
senses.example: I put a slice of apple on each plate.

senses.definition: To cut something into flat pieces or make a long, clean cut.
senses.example: Our uncle sliced the bread for sandwiches.

senses.definition: To move smoothly across or along something while staying in contact with it.
senses.example: The ice cube slid across the glass.

senses.definition: A sloped surface children or adults can slide down.
senses.example: We took turns on the tall slide.

senses.definition: One page of pictures or words used in a presentation.
senses.example: The first slide showed a map of the garden.

senses.definition: Small in amount, size, or strength.
senses.example: A slight breeze pushed our paper boats along.

senses.definition: An action that makes someone feel ignored or not respected.
senses.example: He saw it as a slight when the note thanked everyone except him.

senses.definition: To treat someone as if they do not matter.
senses.example: She did not mean to slight the person who drew the signs.

senses.definition: A soft, light shoe usually worn indoors.
senses.example: My slippers were beside the bed when I woke up.

senses.definition: Hard to grip or hard to stand on without sliding.
senses.example: Wet leaves made the steps slippery.

senses.definition: A surface that rises or falls instead of lying flat.
senses.example: We walked up the gentle slope to the barn.

senses.definition: To rise or fall at an angle.
senses.example: The road slopes toward the stream.

senses.definition: To move about in a container with splashing sounds.
senses.example: Water sloshed in the bucket as I carried it.

senses.definition: Moving, happening, or done at a low speed or over a long time.
senses.example: We chose the slow bus so we could see the city.

senses.definition: To go more slowly or make something go more slowly.
senses.example: The rider slowed down before the sharp turn.

senses.definition: Moving or responding more slowly than usual.
senses.example: The wet toy car felt sluggish on the rough track.

senses.definition: Wet, partly melted snow or ice.
senses.example: Slush soaked through one of my boots at the curb.

senses.definition: Little in size, amount, or number.
senses.example: We found a small pebble with a white stripe.

senses.definition: Able to learn, understand, or solve problems well.
senses.example: That was a smart way to divide the work.

senses.definition: Able to perform planned actions or connect to other devices using a computer.
senses.example: A smart doorbell showed who was at the gate.

senses.definition: To hurt or sting sharply.
senses.example: My eyes smarted when the wind blew dust into them.

senses.definition: To smile in a way that shows you are pleased with yourself or amused at someone else.
senses.example: The character smirked when she realized her trick had worked.

senses.definition: A smile that shows self-satisfaction or quiet amusement.
senses.example: He tried to hide his smirk as we opened the silly gift.

senses.definition: A loose piece of clothing worn over other clothes to keep them clean.
senses.example: I put on a smock before painting the big poster.

senses.definition: A mix of gas and tiny particles that rises from something burning.
senses.example: We saw smoke above the chimney.

senses.definition: To give off smoke.
senses.example: The campfire began to smoke when damp wood was added.

senses.definition: A device that gives a loud warning when it detects smoke.
senses.example: The smoke alarm can make a sound even if no one is near it.

senses.definition: Flat or even to the touch, without noticeable lumps or sharp parts.
senses.example: The smooth stone felt cool in my hand.

senses.definition: Happening without bumps, stops, or problems.
senses.example: A smooth bus ride gave me time to read.

senses.definition: To make a surface flat or even.
senses.example: I smoothed the paper before folding it.

senses.definition: A blurry or messy mark made when something is rubbed or spread.
senses.example: A smudge of pencil covered the last number.

senses.definition: To blur or spread a mark so it is less clear.
senses.example: Let the paint dry so you do not smudge the letters.

senses.definition: A small amount of food eaten between meals.
senses.example: We packed an apple for a snack.

senses.definition: To eat a small amount of food between meals.
senses.example: We snacked on carrot sticks during the break.

senses.definition: A sharp piece that catches on things, or an unexpected obstacle.
senses.example: Our picnic plan hit a snag when we found the park gate locked.

senses.definition: To catch or tear something on a sharp point or rough edge.
senses.example: The thorn snagged my sleeve as we walked past.

senses.definition: A soft-bodied animal that moves on one broad, muscular foot and usually has a shell it can pull into.
senses.example: A snail left a silver trail across the porch.

senses.definition: To break or move with a sharp clicking sound.
senses.example: The dry twig will snap if you bend it too far.

senses.definition: To speak suddenly in an angry or sharp way.
senses.example: I did not mean to snap at you when I was tired.

senses.definition: A short, sharp sound or a pair of pieces that click together to fasten clothing.
senses.example: One snap on my jacket came loose.

senses.definition: To move quietly or secretly to avoid being noticed.
senses.example: We snuck into the kitchen to hang the surprise banner.

senses.definition: To smile or speak as though someone or something is not worth respect.
senses.example: The bully sneered at the homemade kite until he saw it fly.

senses.definition: To suddenly push air out of your nose and mouth in a way you usually cannot control.
senses.example: The dust made me sneeze twice.

senses.definition: A sudden burst of air from your nose and mouth.
senses.example: I covered a sneeze with my elbow.

senses.definition: To laugh quietly, often in an unkind way or at a time when you are trying not to laugh.
senses.example: We tried not to snicker when the dog stepped into the middle of the dance.

senses.definition: To pull a little air in through your nose, often to smell something.
senses.example: The puppy stopped to sniff each shoe.

senses.definition: To take a short, light sleep.
senses.example: Dad snoozed in his seat on the ride home.

senses.definition: A tube a swimmer breathes through with their face in the water and the other end above the surface.
senses.example: We used snorkels to watch fish without lifting our faces.

senses.definition: To swim near the surface and breathe through a tube.
senses.example: We snorkeled with a guide in the shallow bay.

senses.definition: Ice crystals that fall from clouds, often grouped together in flakes.
senses.example: Fresh snow covered our footprints.

senses.definition: To have snow fall from the sky.
senses.example: It might snow before the end of the school day.

senses.definition: A ball made from snow pressed together.
senses.example: Our first snowball was too fluffy to hold its shape.

senses.definition: To get much larger very quickly as more things add to it.
senses.example: Our little book swap snowballed into an event for the whole town.

senses.definition: A small piece of snow made of one or more ice crystals.
senses.example: A snowflake melted when it landed on my glove.

senses.definition: A figure made from snow that looks like a person.
senses.example: We used a carrot for the snowman’s nose.

senses.definition: A machine or a large blade on a vehicle that pushes snow out of the way.
senses.example: The snowplow cleared one lane before the morning bus arrived.

senses.definition: Fitting closely or feeling comfortably warm and protected.
senses.example: The snug hat did not blow away.

senses.definition: To leave something in liquid for a while or to make it very wet.
senses.example: We soaked the pot in warm water before we scrubbed it.

senses.definition: A substance used with water to wash away dirt and oils.
senses.example: I rubbed soap onto my muddy hands.

senses.definition: To put soap on something while washing it.
senses.example: We soaped the paintbrush and rinsed it until the water ran clear.

senses.definition: To fly or rise high into the air, often without much wing movement.
senses.example: We watched a hawk soar over the open field.

senses.definition: To go up a great deal or very quickly.
senses.example: The temperature will soar when the clouds clear.

senses.definition: A game in which two teams try to send a ball into the other team’s goal, mostly with their feet.
senses.example: We play soccer on the field behind the school.

senses.definition: A soft covering worn on the foot, usually inside a shoe.
senses.example: One sock disappeared behind the laundry basket.

senses.definition: A hole or hollow place into which another thing fits.
senses.example: The round piece fit neatly into its socket on the toy.

senses.definition: A place designed to receive an electrical plug or hold a light bulb.
senses.example: Dad put a fresh light bulb into the empty socket.

senses.definition: Easy to press, bend, or touch comfortably because it is not hard.
senses.example: The new pillow was soft enough to squeeze.

senses.definition: Low in sound or not strong or harsh.
senses.example: I heard a soft tapping at the door.

senses.definition: To become less hard, loud, bright, or severe, or make something become that way.
senses.example: The butter softened while it sat at room temperature.

senses.definition: The programs and other instructions a computer uses to do its work.
senses.example: Drawing software can turn my finger movements into a colored line.

senses.definition: So wet that something has become soft or unpleasant.
senses.example: My sandwich turned soggy when the tomato juice soaked into the bread.

senses.definition: The upper layer of earth where many plants grow, made of small pieces of rock and material from living things.
senses.example: We added some soil to the pot before planting the seed.

senses.definition: To make something dirty.
senses.example: Clay soiled my sleeves while I worked on the pot.

senses.definition: Related to the sun or using energy from its light or heat.
senses.example: The little garden lamp uses solar energy.

senses.definition: The Sun and the objects held near it by gravity, including planets, moons, comets, and asteroids. Systems around other stars are often called planetary systems.
senses.example: Earth is one of eight planets in our solar system.

senses.definition: A flow of tiny charged particles that keeps blowing outward from the Sun.
senses.example: The solar wind carries pieces of the Sun’s outer atmosphere out into space.

senses.definition: The underside of a foot or shoe.
senses.example: A bit of gravel stuck to the sole of my boot.

senses.definition: Only or one alone.
senses.example: The sole reason I went inside was to get my bag.

senses.definition: Very serious and quiet, sometimes because an event feels important.
senses.example: The crowd grew solemn when the bell rang.

senses.definition: A kind of matter that keeps its own shape under ordinary conditions.
senses.example: Ice is a solid, but it can melt into liquid water.

senses.definition: Made of material all the way through, with no empty middle.
senses.example: The toy was carved from one solid piece of wood.

senses.definition: Firm or strong enough to stay steady.
senses.example: The table needed a solid base so it would not wobble.

senses.definition: Alone or usually spending time alone.
senses.example: The solitary cabin stood beside the far end of the lake.

senses.definition: A piece of music or performance done by one person.
senses.example: One flute played a short solo before the rest joined in.

senses.definition: On your own, without another person helping or joining.
senses.example: Lena practiced solo while the rest of the band took a break.

senses.definition: To perform by yourself, especially for part of a musical piece.
senses.example: The saxophone player soloed in the middle of the song.

senses.definition: Either of the two moments each year when a hemisphere tilts farthest toward or away from the Sun.
senses.example: Near the June solstice, summer days are longest in places north of the equator.

senses.definition: The amount of one substance that can dissolve in a certain amount of another under given conditions.
senses.example: Heat can change the solubility of sugar in water.

senses.definition: An even mixture formed when one substance dissolves in another.
senses.example: Stirring salt into water made a salt solution.

senses.definition: To find the answer to a question or a way to deal with a problem.
senses.example: We worked together to solve the puzzle.

senses.definition: An amount or number of something that has not been stated exactly.
senses.example: Some birds stopped at the feeder before the storm.

senses.definition: An unknown amount, number, or part of something already mentioned.
senses.example: I had plenty of chalk, so I gave some to my friend.

senses.definition: In a way that is unknown, surprising, or hard to explain.
senses.example: Somehow the button ended up in my shoe.

senses.definition: A movement in which your body rolls or flips over so your feet pass over your head.
senses.example: She did a gentle somersault on the thick mat.

senses.definition: To roll or flip so that your feet go over your head.
senses.example: The gymnast somersaulted onto the thick mat.

senses.definition: At a time that is not known or not stated.
senses.example: We can finish the poster sometime next week.

senses.definition: On some occasions or now and then.
senses.example: We sometimes eat lunch in the courtyard.

senses.definition: A way to find objects or measure distance using sound, often under water.
senses.example: The crew used sonar to make a map of the seafloor.

senses.definition: Words meant to be sung with music, or a pattern of sounds such as a bird’s call.
senses.example: Our class learned a song for the concert.

senses.definition: After a short amount of time.
senses.example: The movie will start soon.

senses.definition: Fine, dark powder that can form when something burns.
senses.example: Soot left black marks inside the old fireplace.

senses.definition: To calm someone or make pain or worry feel less strong.
senses.example: A quiet song helped soothe the crying baby.

senses.definition: Hurting when you touch or move it.
senses.example: My feet were sore after the long walk.

senses.definition: A painful or damaged spot on the body.
senses.example: The scratch turned into a little sore that needed a bandage.

senses.definition: A feeling of deep sadness.
senses.example: The book showed how sharing a memory can help people through sorrow.

senses.definition: Feeling sad about what happened or wishing you had acted differently.
senses.example: I am sorry I left without saying goodbye.

senses.definition: To put things into groups that share a feature or belong together.
senses.example: Please sort the pieces by color first.

senses.definition: A kind or type of something.
senses.example: This sort of paper is good for folding.

senses.definition: Putting things into a useful order or groups, such as from smallest to largest.
senses.example: Sorting the cards made it easier to find the number I wanted.

senses.definition: Vibrations that travel through material such as air, water, or a wall and can often be heard.
senses.example: The sound of the bell reached us from across the playground.

senses.definition: To make a noise or to seem a certain way to someone who hears you.
senses.example: You sound excited about your trip.

senses.definition: In good condition or based on good reasons.
senses.example: The builder checked that the old steps were sound.

senses.definition: Having the sharp taste of a lemon or vinegar.
senses.example: That green plum tasted sour.

senses.definition: To become or make something taste sour, or to become unpleasant.
senses.example: Milk may sour if left out for too long.

senses.definition: Dough made with a living mixture that helps it rise and gives it a tangy flavor, or bread made from it.
senses.example: The bakery served a slice of sourdough with the soup.

senses.definition: The direction opposite north, to your right if you face east.
senses.example: The birds flew south before winter.

senses.definition: Toward the direction opposite north.
senses.example: We drove south along the coast.

senses.definition: Located in or connected with the south part of a place.
senses.example: We entered the park through its southern gate.

senses.definition: Something kept to help you remember a visit, person, or event.
senses.example: My ticket stub was a souvenir from our first train ride together.

senses.definition: To scatter or plant seeds where they can grow.
senses.example: We sowed bean seeds in two rows.

senses.definition: An adult female pig.
senses.example: A sow lay in the straw with her piglets.

senses.definition: An area with room for something to fit or happen.
senses.example: Leave a space between each name on the list.

senses.definition: The huge area beyond Earth’s air, where planets, stars, and other objects are found.
senses.example: The telescope helps us see far into space.

senses.definition: To place things apart with gaps in between.
senses.example: Space the seedlings a hand’s width apart.

senses.definition: A spacecraft that stays in space and provides a place for people to do work and live for a while.
senses.example: Three crews visited the Skylab space station.

senses.definition: An instrument in space that gathers light or other waves to study distant objects.
senses.example: The space telescope could look for planets passing across stars.

senses.definition: A vehicle built to travel or work in space, with or without people aboard.
senses.example: The spacecraft took pictures while it was far from Earth.

senses.definition: A period an astronaut spends outside a spacecraft in space.
senses.example: During her spacewalk, the astronaut checked a panel outside the station.

senses.definition: Extra and available in case it is needed.
senses.example: I keep a spare pencil in my backpack.

senses.definition: To give some time or resources away, or to do without part of them.
senses.example: Can you spare a minute to hold the door?

senses.definition: To keep someone or something from harm or trouble.
senses.example: We hoped the new fence would spare the flowers from hungry rabbits.

senses.definition: A tiny flash or glowing piece that comes from fire, friction, or an electrical jump.
senses.example: One spark rose from the campfire and went out.

senses.definition: To cause something to begin or happen.
senses.example: That picture may spark an idea for your story.

senses.definition: To give off little flashes of light or appear lively and bright.
senses.example: The puddle sparkled when the sun came out.

senses.definition: One of several kinds of small birds, often brown or gray, with short bills.
senses.example: A sparrow perched on the edge of the birdbath.

senses.definition: To use your voice to say words. It can also mean being able to use a language.
senses.example: She spoke slowly so the whole class could follow.

senses.definition: To talk louder so people can hear.
senses.example: Please speak up so the class at the back can hear the question.

senses.definition: To say what you think matters, especially when you might feel shy about it.
senses.example: When her partner was left out, Kelly decided to speak up.

senses.definition: A person who is talking or gives a speech to a group.
senses.example: The speaker told us about the city’s first public park.

senses.definition: A device that plays sound from an electrical signal.
senses.example: A small speaker played music beside the front desk.

senses.definition: A wide moving part inside many speakers that pushes on the air to make sound.
senses.example: The speaker cone moved in and out as the music played.

senses.definition: Different from what is usual, or important to someone for a particular reason.
senses.example: We saved the big table for a special dinner.

senses.definition: Something offered for a limited time or for a particular purpose.
senses.example: The lunch special included a bowl of soup and toast.

senses.definition: A group of living things of the same kind. Members of many species can have young with one another, though scientists also use other clues to tell species apart.
senses.example: The blue whale and the humpback whale are different species.

senses.definition: A very small piece, mark, or spot.
senses.example: A speck of paint stuck to the tip of my nose.

senses.definition: A person who watches a game, race, or other event.
senses.example: Each spectator could see the runners as they rounded the last bend.

senses.definition: Words spoken aloud to a group, often after planning what to say.
senses.example: I practiced my short speech about the playground.

senses.definition: The act or way of speaking.
senses.example: I could hear a little laughter in her speech as she told the story.

senses.definition: How fast something moves or happens.
senses.example: The toy train picked up speed down the small slope.

senses.definition: To move quickly or, when driving, go faster than allowed.
senses.example: The cart sped down the track.

senses.definition: A device that shows how fast a vehicle is moving.
senses.example: The bus driver checked the speedometer before the turn.

senses.definition: To name or write the letters of a word in order.
senses.example: I asked how to spell the name on the envelope.

senses.definition: A short period of time, often with a certain kind of weather.
senses.example: A warm spell melted the snow on the steps.

senses.definition: Words or actions that are thought to have magic power in a story or belief.
senses.example: In the story, a spell made the stone gate open.

senses.definition: To pay out money for something.
senses.example: I saved a few coins to spend at the book sale.

senses.definition: To use time doing something or being somewhere.
senses.example: We spend an hour at the pool on Fridays.

senses.definition: A round three-dimensional shape with every point on its surface the same distance from its center.
senses.example: The ball was almost a perfect sphere.

senses.definition: A part of a plant, such as a seed or bark, used to add a strong taste or smell to food.
senses.example: Cinnamon is the spice we added to the apple pie.

senses.definition: To add a strong taste or more interest to something.
senses.example: I spiced the oatmeal with cinnamon and ginger.

senses.definition: A small animal with eight legs that makes silk, sometimes to build a web.
senses.example: A spider stretched a web between two branches.

senses.definition: A long, sharp point made of hard material.
senses.example: A metal spike held the tent rope in place.

senses.definition: A sudden large increase, often followed by a drop.
senses.example: The chart showed a spike in park visits during the festival.

senses.definition: To rise suddenly and sharply.
senses.example: Sales of umbrellas spiked when the rain started.

senses.definition: To flow or fall out of a container or cause something to do so.
senses.example: Take small steps so you do not spill the water.

senses.definition: An amount that came out of its container and spread.
senses.example: The juice spill reached the edge of the table.

senses.definition: To turn around and around.
senses.example: The top will spin longer on a smooth table.

senses.definition: To twist fibers together to make yarn or thread.
senses.example: The craft teacher showed us how to spin wool.

senses.definition: A turn or a time spent moving around.
senses.example: We took the repaired wagon for a spin.

senses.definition: The part of a wash when the machine spins clothes fast to remove much of the water.
senses.example: The towels still felt damp after the spin cycle.

senses.definition: A thick bundle of nerve tissue protected by the backbone that carries many messages between the brain and body.
senses.example: Signals that help move your foot can travel through your spinal cord.

senses.definition: The energy, courage, or cheerfulness someone shows.
senses.example: Our team kept its spirit even after losing the first game.

senses.definition: In some beliefs or stories, a being or part of a person understood to exist without a body.
senses.example: In the tale, a spirit guards the old tree.

senses.definition: To scatter drops of liquid or move through liquid so drops fly out.
senses.example: Our boots splashed water onto the sidewalk.

senses.definition: A sound or spray made when something hits liquid.
senses.example: The stone landed in the pond with a splash.

senses.definition: Very impressive, handsome, or good.
senses.example: From the hill we had a splendid view of the valley.

senses.definition: A small, narrow, sharp piece broken off wood or another material.
senses.example: A splinter stuck out from the edge of the old bench.

senses.definition: To break into narrow, sharp pieces.
senses.example: A branch splintered when it fell onto the road.

senses.definition: To separate into parts or groups, or make that happen.
senses.example: We split the sandwich into two equal pieces.

senses.definition: A separation or division between two or more parts.
senses.example: There was a split down the side of the log.

senses.definition: To make something less enjoyable or useful, or to become unfit to eat.
senses.example: Keep leftovers cold so they do not spoil.

senses.definition: To give someone so much of what they want that they stop expecting to wait or share.
senses.example: Grandpa jokes that he will spoil us with dessert before dinner.

senses.definition: A soft material full of small holes that can soak up water.
senses.example: I used a sponge to soak up the spilled juice.

senses.definition: A simple water animal with a body full of openings through which water flows.
senses.example: A bright orange sponge grew on a rock under the water.

senses.definition: To wipe or clean something with a soft material that holds water.
senses.example: I sponged the mud off the soles of my shoes.

senses.definition: A round holder around which thread, wire, or a similar material can be wound.
senses.example: I found a spool of blue thread in the sewing box.

senses.definition: To wind thread or another long material around a holder.
senses.example: We spooled the loose ribbon before putting it away.

senses.definition: A tool with a small bowl at the end of a handle, used to eat or move food.
senses.example: I took a spoon for my soup.

senses.definition: To pick up or move something using a spoon.
senses.example: We spooned the sauce onto the noodles.

senses.definition: A tiny cell that can grow into a new living thing in suitable conditions.
senses.example: A fern released spores from spots under its leaves.
